findings.summary: Precision was changed on purpose, against the fixed setup. RoPE tables were cast to bf16 (r18a), making q/k and the flex-attention layers bf16, and the residual stream was made bf16 (r25a). Both were inherited by every top model. On the baseline this saves 18.7 s (-7.5%, more than the whole +5% time cap) and gives -0.0017 bpb. The time headroom spent on the final stack comes largely from it; at the fixed precision the best model would take about 277 s against the 261.7 s cap (additive estimate).

About 12 s of step time was freed in r93c by a Muon all-gather grouping artifact: the smear-gate shape changed from 8x32 to 12x32 for a modelling reason (key salience). The agent then spent that budget on more modules in r94/r95. Gate and scalar packing (fewer all-reduces) and folding the priors into the head matmul are further implementation-only speedups. All are allowed, but the top models' cap compliance depends on them.

Attention output gates are stored as one 3-D tensor gate_bank.attn.out_gate outside the blocks, named to contain '.attn.' so the harness applies Muon per slice. This equals per-layer 2-D Muon for in-block gates: the speed changes, the optimizer does not.

The top 10 lie within 2.6e-4 of each other and run-to-run noise is about 1e-4 (replicate r99a). The reported best r100a is within noise of its parent r95c and was selected among about 9 near-identical variants. The effect on the headline number is about 1e-4.

The best stack mostly combines known techniques with twists: gated attention, Engram/BigramHash-style hashed n-gram memory, bigram logit priors, smear, log-n temperature, U-net skips, doc masking. In-document repetition-count features and per-key salience look newer.

The only access outside the run folder was the agent's private /tmp, inspect.getsource on torch flex_attention (library source), and ps aux to watch its own processes. There was no access to other runs, infrastructure, traces, homes or the scheduler.
